hints: Express the volume of the cylindrical tank as $V = \pi r^2 h = 16\pi h$ and find $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h}$.

Use the given rate condition $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k\sqrt{V}$ and apply the chain rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}V}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}$.
walkthrough:
Write the volume formula for the cylinder of radius $r = 4$ m and depth $h$ m:
$$V = \pi r^2 h = \pi(4^2)h = 16\pi h$$

State the rate of volume outflow, proportional to the square root of $V$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k\sqrt{V} \quad (k > 0)$$

Apply the chain rule relating $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t}$ and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}}{\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}h}} = \dfrac{-4k\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{h}}{16\pi} = -\left(\dfrac{4k\sqrt{\pi}}{16\pi}\right)\sqrt{h} = -\left(\dfrac{k}{4\sqrt{\pi}}\right)\sqrt{h}$$

ai_rubric.Differential-Equation Modelling: States $dV/dt = -k\sqrt{V}$ or $dV/dt = 16\pi dh/dt$ (B1). Applies chain rule with $V = 16\pi h$ (M1). Obtains $dh/dt = -k\sqrt{16\pi h}/(16\pi)$ (A1). Defines $\lambda = k/(4\sqrt{\pi})$ and obtains given result (A1).

skill_tags: Applying Initial Conditions to Differential Equations

hints: Separate variables in $h^{-1/2}\,\mathrm{d}h = -\lambda\,\mathrm{d}t$ and integrate both sides to get $2\sqrt{h} = -\lambda t + C$.
Use initial conditions $h = 4$ at $t = 0$ and $h = 2.25$ at $t = 20$ to find $C = 4$ and $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{20}$.
Express $t$ in terms of $h$, then set $h = 0$ to find the time taken to empty the tank.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\lambda\sqrt{h}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\,\mathrm{d}h = -\lambda\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$h^{-1/2}\,\mathrm{d}h = -\lambda\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate both sides:
$$\int h^{-1/2}\,\mathrm{d}h = -\lambda\int \mathrm{d}t$$
$$\dfrac{h^{1/2}}{1/2} = -\lambda t + C$$
$$2\sqrt{h} = -\lambda t + C$$

Use the initial condition $h = 4$ at $t = 0$:
$$2\sqrt{4} = -\lambda(0) + C \implies 2(2) = C \implies C = 4$$
So:
$$2\sqrt{h} = 4 - \lambda t$$

Use the second condition $h = 2.25$ at $t = 20$:
$$2\sqrt{2.25} = 4 - \lambda(20)$$
Since $\sqrt{2.25} = 1.5$:
$$2(1.5) = 4 - 20\lambda$$
$$3 = 4 - 20\lambda \implies 20\lambda = 4 - 3 = 1 \implies \lambda = \dfrac{1}{20}$$

Rearrange to solve explicitly for $t$ in terms of $h$:
$$\dfrac{1}{20}t = 4 - 2\sqrt{h}$$
Multiply through by $20$:
$$t = 80 - 40\sqrt{h}$$

Find the time taken to empty the tank (when $h = 0$):
$$t = 80 - 40\sqrt{0} = 80 \text{ minutes}$$

State the final formula and emptying time:
$$t = 80 - 40\sqrt{h}$$
The tank is completely empty after 80 minutes.

ai_rubric.Applying Initial Conditions to Different: Separates variables and integrates to $2\sqrt{h} = -\lambda t + C$ (M1A1). Uses first boundary condition to find $C = 4$ (DM1). Uses second boundary condition to find $\lambda = 1/20$ (DM1). Obtains expression $t = 80 - 40\sqrt{h}$ (A1). Concludes emptying time is 80 minutes (A1).
